decision_maker: Council
content:
Council approved the following recommendation:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendation of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendation approved.
 
RESOLVED:
That the Council adopt the Statement of Licensing
Policy 2026.
 
Reason for Decisions:
 
Responsibility for adopting the
Statement of Licensing Policy rests with Full Council as part of
the Council's Policy Framework.

Council approved the following recommendation:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendations of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendations approved.
 
RESOLVED:
 
1)   
That Full Council:
 
i)               
Approved the proposed constitutional changes
required to reflect Government changes to the planning system as
set out in section 4 and in Appendix A of the report;
and
 
ii)              
Approved the proposed constitutional changes
required to the Scheme of Delegations to Officers as set out in
section 4 and Appendix C of the report.
 
2)   
That Full Council noted the proposed scope and
timetable for the wider review of the Constitution.
 
Reasons for
Decision:
 

1)    
Changes to the Council’s Constitution are required to
implement the Government’s new National Scheme of Delegation
for planning functions and the introduction of the post of Chief
Operating Officer. The Government has introduced a new National
Scheme of Delegation for planning functions, alongside rules on the
size of planning committees. These regulations were laid in
Parliament on 15 July, and the changes will come into force on 31
October 2026. Proposed changes are outlined in Section 4 and set
out in full in Appendices A and C.
 

2)    
The Council is required under section 9P of the Local Government
Act 2000 to prepare and keep up to date its Constitution. The Local
Government Act 2000 (Constitutions) (England) Direction 2000 also
prescribes matters that must be included within the Constitution.
Although the Constitution has been updated on a piecemeal basis
over time, a more structured review is now appropriate to ensure
that it remains legally compliant, clear, accessible, up to date
and aligned with good governance practice, including transparent
decision-making and clear lines of responsibility.
 

3)    
The Council’s Constitution is central to effective governance
and decision making. It defines the Council’s decision-making
structures, the respective roles of members and officers, the
procedures for meetings and the framework through which
transparency, accountability and lawful decision-making are
secured. A review is proposed to ensure that the Constitution
remains up to date, clear and fit for purpose.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member  for City Management
content:
Summary of
Decision
 
The Cabinet Member for City Management has
approved the award of concession contracts for an initial term of
four years from 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2030, with provision
to extend by up to two further years, for the Parking Debt
Management Service to:
 
• CDER Group Limited
• Marston (Holdings) Limited
• Newlyn PLC
 
Reasons for
Decision
 
The Council requires a continued Parking Debt
Management Service to support the statutory recovery of unpaid
Penalty Charge Notices. The current single-operator arrangement
expires on 31 October 2026. Awarding the proposed contracts will
allow the new service to commence on 1 November 2026 and avoid a
gap in provision.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Enforcement

Decision
 
The Cabinet Member for Enforcement has
approved the adoption of
the Food Safety Service Plan 2026-27 on behalf
of Westminster City Council.
 
Reasons for
Decision
 
The Food Safety Service Plan sets out how
Westminster City Council meets its statutory obligations in line
with the food law code of practice. Adoption of the plan will
ensure that the Council continues to fulfil its statutory
responsibilities for food law enforcement, supports
the Council's commitment to protecting residents, workers and
visitors and provides a clear framework for delivering
interventions during 2026/27.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning
content:
Summary of
Decision
 
The Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning has
approved the re-designation of the Marylebone Neighbourhood Forum
for a further period of five years and has authorised the Director
of Policy and Strategy to formally publish a designation
notice.
 
Reasons for
Decision
 
Section 61F of the Act sets out the conditions
that the council must be satisfied a prospective neighbourhood
forum meets to be designated. The Act also stipulates further
considerations that the council must have regard to when making
this decision. It is considered that Marylebone Neighbourhood Forum
meets all the prescribed conditions, as evidenced by their
application and as set out in the Cabinet Member Report.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning has decided to approve the re-designation of the Marylebone Neighbourhood Forum for a further five years

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning
content:
Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning
has
accepted the Examiner’s recommendations, as
set out in the Examiner’s Report and has agreed
that the Notting Hill East Neighbourhood Plan,
as modified, proceeds to
local referendum. The Cabinet Member has also agreed that
the referendum area be restricted to the Notting Hill
East Neighbourhood Area, and that in the event
of a positive referendum result, the Director
of Policy and Strategy be authorised to publish an Adoption
Statement and formally ‘make’ (adopt) the
plan. 
 
Reasons for
Decision
The Examiner’s recommended
modifications will ensure the Notting Hill East
Neighbourhood Plan is clear and effective as a framework for
making planning decisions in the Notting Hill
East Neighbourhood Area.  The
recommendations address the concerns raised by
the council and several other
stakeholders received during Regulation
16 consultation. They will also
ensure the plan meets all legal
requirements needed to progress to referendum.
Accepting the examiner’s recommendations and proceeding to
referendum will ensure
the council fulfils its statutory responsibility under
the Localism Act 2011 to assist local communities
in exercising their neighbourhood planning powers
effectively.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning has decided to proceed with the Notting Hill East Neighbourhood Plan to local referendum.

content:
Council approved the following recommendation:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendation of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendation approved.
 
Resolved:
          
That Full Council:
 
1)
       approved
the amended Members’ Allowances Scheme for 2026–2027,
as set out in Appendix A, with effect from 20 May 2026;
and
 
2)
       noted
that elected Members are eligible to join the Local Government
Pension Scheme (LGPS) from 11 May 2026.
 
Reasons for Decision:
 
The amendments to the Scheme provides for the following
changes to the committee structure: 
 

the introduction of
an additional Policy and Scrutiny Committee, the Chair of
which will be eligible for an SRA; 

 

the establishment of
an additional Planning Sub-Committee, resulting in
two additional Members being eligible for a Planning SRA;
and 

 

a reduction in the
membership of both the Discretionary Housing Payment Panel and the
Ratings Panel from five to four Members, reducing the number of
SRA-eligible positions on each body by one.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the amended Members' Allowances Scheme for 2026-2027 and allow elected Members to join the Local Government Pension Scheme.

2)
      approved the
proposed amendments to the Task Group provisions set out in Chapter
4 of the Constitution, clarifying the role of the Overview and
Scrutiny Committee in establishing and overseeing Task
Groups;
 
3)
      approved the
proposed minor amendments to Chapter 4 of the Constitution to
ensure consistency and accuracy of the Chapter as a whole;
and
 
4)
      noted that the
Director of Law would keep under review the operation and
effectiveness of the constitution, including the provisions
proposed for amendment within the report, and would bring back to
full council, via the General Purposes Committee, any proposals for
change as soon as possible after the need for change was
identified.
 
Reason for Decisions:
 

1)             
Following changes approved by Full Council to the
size and structure of Policy and Scrutiny Committees, consequential
amendments to the Council’s Constitution were
proposed. 
 

2)             
These included reducing the threshold required to
exercise call-in from three Members to two Members of the relevant
Policy and Scrutiny Committee, to ensure that the call-in
mechanism remained proportionate, accessible and effective. 
 
3)       The
report also proposed the introduction of criteria for when and
why a decision may be subject to call-in. These criteria promoted
consistency in the application of call-in and supported
the Council’s scrutiny function to focus on strategic
oversight.  
 
4)      
Amendments to the existing provisions with regards
to Task Groups was also proposed to provide for
oversight and approval of Task Groups by the Overview and Scrutiny
Committee, supporting a more coordinated and effective approach to
scrutiny. 
 
5)      
Minor amendments to Chapter 4 of the constitution were also
proposed to ensure the overall consistency and accuracy of the
Council’s policy and scrutiny arrangements.
topline: The Council has decided to approve amendments to the call-in procedure, Task Group provisions, and minor amendments to the Constitution for consistency and accuracy.

decision_maker: Executive Director for Environment and Communities
content:
The Executive Director of
Environment and Communities has approved Transport for London (TfL)
undertaking works comprising changes to a number of streets in the
area surrounding the extents of the TfL Oxford Street West (OSW)
proposals, including the Making of associated Traffic Management
Orders under the Road Traffic Regulation Act (1984) and TfL
undertaking works on Westminster highway in support of the changes
by entering into legal agreements pursuant to Section 101 of the
Local Government Action (1972) and Section 8 of the Highways Act
(1980).
 
Section 101
of the Local Government Act 1972 (LGA 1972)
gives local authorities in England and Wales the statutory power to
delegate their responsibilities. It allows a council to arrange for
its functions to be discharged by a committee, a sub-committee, an
officer, or even another local authority
 
Section 8 of the Highways
Act 1980 enables local highway
authorities and the national government to enter into formal legal
agreements. These agreements allow one authority to carry out
construction, improvement, or maintenance functions on behalf of
another authority.

content:
Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
Public Health, and Voluntary Sector has approved the award
of the contracts set out in the Cabinet Member Report for?the
provision of?Learning Disabilities Housing, Care and
Support?services?for?a?period of?5 years?with an anticipated start
date of 1 April 2026, and with?two optional extensions of 3 years
and 2 years (total contract period of up to 10 years).
 
Reasons for
Decision
 The Council has a statutory duty under
the Care Act 2014 to ensure appropriate personalised care
and support to meet the individual assessed needs of Service Users
and maximise independence, focusing on choice and control for
people in receipt of Learning Disability Services, ensure
consistency and continuity of care, minimising service disruption
for vulnerable adults with learning disabilities living in the
community and actively shape the market to ensure diversity and
quality in care services and implement fair pricing strategies that
reflect that the actual cost of care, ensuring that all providers
can compete equitably and sustainably. These contracts will enable
the Council to meet its statutory duties.

decision_maker: Shareholder Committee
content:
Cllr Hug welcomed Joe Smith, Zohaib Nizami and
Georgina Nash to the meeting and invited them to introduce the
report.
 
Joe Smith provided an overview of the business
plan and objectives of the company. Joe thanked James Green for his
contribution to the company following his resignation. Sales at
Luton St have been fully completed, allowing the progress of
dissolution of the JV. A major milestone this year was gaining
Cabinet approval for Ebury Phase 2 to be delivered through WHDL.
The company has also proceeded with applying for RP status for
WHPL. Westminster Builds has stable finances despite a challenging
global economic picture.
 
Zohaib said that the draft financial outturn
will come to the next meeting and that the companies financial
position remains robust.
 
Cllr Boothroyd asked for an update on RP
status. Joe replied that it remains a long-term strategic aim for
the company and that the company is progressing and mitigations
have been put in place to protect against loss of grants.
 
Cllr Hug asked about the reasoning for
Westminster Builds delivering the Ebury Phase 2 scheme. Georgina
Nash explained that this means the HRA does not have to bear the
cost of the development and would not have received payment back
until the private properties would have been sold. This approach
means the cost can be shared and neither fund comes under undue
financial pressure.
 
Cllr Ormsby asked about how the team has been
prepared for managing a growing portfolio. Joe replied that the
management team is meeting more regularly, regularly reviewing the
pipeline and anticipating risk in the current economic climate. The
company is also working closely with Council teams and flagging any
issues early in processes. Zohaib added that the company’s
financial modelling has improved.
 
Cllr Ormsby asked how the company has been
impacted by the Renters’ Rights Act. Joe said that work is
being done to understand the any implications of the Act on income
thresholds.
 
Cllr Hug asked the Committee to approve the
business plan for Westminster Builds. The business plan was
approved.
topline: The Shareholder Committee has decided to approve the business plan for Westminster Builds.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider a new Housing Strategy
for Westminster which sets out the direction of travel over the
next few years.
content:
Cabinet will consider a new Housing Strategy
for Westminster which sets out the direction of travel over the
next few years.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

·      
To approve the Westminster Housing Strategy 2026-2031 (Appendix
A).
 

·      
To delegate authority to the Executive Director of Housing and
Commercial Partnerships to make minor amendments to the Westminster
Housing Strategy 2026-2031 and its actions if they are
required.
 
Reasons for
decision:
 

·      
An overarching Housing Strategy was recommended by the Future of
Westminster Commission to provide a framework for council
initiatives and this will help the Council meet its Fairer
Westminster Strategy and to achieve the aim of Fairer Housing.
 

·      
The Strategy is also needed to:
o  
Identify the Council’s strategic housing priorities for the
next five years - i.e. the areas of focus - which will be used as a
framework for future plans;
o  
Illustrate the housing policy changes already made and why,
bringing together existing housing policies and strategies and
showing where more information on them can be found;
o  
Set out some of the actions (in the ‘What we will do
next’ sections) that will be taken to help meet the
priorities; and
o  
Show how the housing priorities proposed are often interlinked and
together provide an overall narrative for housing in
Westminster.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Westminster Housing Strategy 2026-2031, setting out the direction of housing initiatives for the next five years.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the review of the scheme
and results of consultation and decide whether to renew the
designation.
content:
Cabinet will consider the review of the scheme
and results of consultation and decide whether to renew the
designation.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

After considering the evidence in
Appendices 1 to 4, and in accordance with Section 56 of the Housing
Act 2024, to approve the making of a new five-year designation to
continue borough-wide Additional HMO Licensing for all Section 254
HMOs not already subject to Mandatory HMO Licensing, to take effect
upon either expiry of the current scheme on 30 August 2026 or a
later date as required to comply with statutory notification
requirements.

 

To approve the proposed scheme
objectives (Appendix 5), the proposed licensing conditions which
will apply to all Section 254 HMOs including those subject to
mandatory licensing(Appendix 6), and the
proposed fee structure (Appendix 7) with its introduction of a
discount to incentivise landlords of the most energy efficient
properties (A-C EPC rating).

 

To delegate authority to the
Director of Public Protection and Licensing, in conjunction with
the City Solicitor, to prepare and issue the formal designation and
public notice for the renewed Additional HMO Licensing Scheme.

 

To delegate authority to the
Director of Public Protection and Licensing to ensure full
compliance with all legal and governance obligations, including the
statutory three-month notice period, and to make minor amendments
and modifications to the scheme during its lifetime, including
adjustments to licence conditions, to ensure the effective delivery
and operation of the scheme.

 
Reasons for
Decision:
 

The current scheme has led to
significant improvements in housing conditions and management
standards across over 2,400 licensed HMOs.

 

This regulatory approach has enabled
the Council to proactively target known risks in a high-pressure
housing market, and to protect vulnerable tenants, many of whom are
on low incomes or have limited housing options.

 

Renewal of the Additional HMO
Licensing Scheme is essential to maintain and build upon the
significant improvements achieved since 2021. Despite progress,
evidence demonstrates that a substantial proportion of HMOs remain
unlicensed and present serious safety and management risks,
including Category 1 hazards under the Housing Health and Safety
Rating System (HHSRS). Continuing the scheme will enable the
Council to proactively regulate these properties, protect
vulnerable tenants, and uphold housing standards in a high-pressure
market where alternative interventions would be insufficient to
address the scale and complexity of the issues identified.

 

The proposed renewal also comes at a
pivotal time when national and local measures are converging to
strengthen regulatory oversight. The introduction of a national
landlords’ database through the Renters’ Rights Act,
combined with Westminster’s recently introduced Selective
Licensing scheme, will significantly enhance the cCouncil’s intelligence capabilities. These
tools will provide improved access to landlord and property data,
enabling more accurate identification of unlicensed HMOs and
facilitating targeted enforcement against non-compliant operators.
This integrated approach will ensure that the renewed Additional
Licensing Scheme operates within a more robust framework,
delivering greater efficiency and impact in tackling housing
risks.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to renew the borough-wide Additional HMO Licensing scheme to improve housing conditions and protect vulnerable tenants.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider NCIL funding allocations following
the Winter Round 2026.
content:
Cabinet will consider NCIL funding allocations following
the Winter Round 2026.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

To approve £250,000 of NCIL
funding from the Bayswater neighbourhood area towards the WCC
Strategic Transport and Connectivity Informal Side?Road Zebra
Crossings.

 
Reasons for
Decision:
 

The Council is required to allocate
NCIL funds with regards to the local priorities set out in
Westminster’s Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Spending
Policy Statement (October 2022), as well as national legislation
and regulations.

 

The Informal Side?Road Zebra
Crossings project proposes the installation of at least 20 new
informal zebra crossings at various side?road junctions across the
Bayswater ward. The scheme delivers low?cost, high?impact
pedestrian safety improvements by applying non?prescribed zebra
markings at junctions where pedestrians currently face poor
visibility and low driver yielding. These informal zebras do not
require full signalisation, making them quick to install and
cost?effective. The proposal follows the Council’s recent
trial across 11 locations, where the markings were shown to
significantly improve pedestrian safety and user confidence.

 

This project is required due to
pedestrians in Bayswater currently face challenging and often
unsafe conditions when crossing side?road junctions. Following the
installation of informal zebra markings at trial sites, there was a
clear and consistent improvement in how drivers behaved, with
significantly more of them stopping for pedestrians.

 

The project aligns with the
Council’s CIL Spending Policy, particularly in supporting
safer, more accessible neighbourhoods. It directly advances the
priority of Sustainable and Active Travel, as the new informal
crossings make walking easier and safer, encouraging people to
choose active modes rather than relying on vehicles. The project
also supports Accessible and Inclusive Public Spaces because the
design includes features that improve safety and independence for
vulnerable pedestrians, such as dropped kerbs and tactile paving.
These elements help ensure that all road users can move around the
area more confidently.

 

It was agreed that recommendation
2.1 would be withdrawn and a revised proposal brought back to a
future meeting of Cabinet.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to allocate £250,000 of NCIL funding towards installing informal zebra crossings in Bayswater for pedestrian safety improvements.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector
purpose:
The Cabinet Member will consider a contract
award for local Genitourinary Medicine (GUM) services.
content:
The Cabinet Member will consider a contract
award for local Genitourinary Medicine (GUM) services.

Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
Public Health and Voluntary Sector has approved that the
Council enter into an Inter-Authority Agreement with City of
London Corporation (CoLC) to
enable WCC residents to access a range of sexual and
reproductive health services, which includes the testing and
treatment of sexually transmitted infections (STI), instead of
procuring its own contract, at an estimated payment of
£7,245,740 to CoLC over 9 years. The Cabinet Member for
Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has
approved that the Council enters into a fresh partnership
agreement with CoLC for the
management of the overall Sexual Health London Partnership, at
a cost of £225,176, over
the nine-year life of the
agreement, for CoLC’s staffing and other
costs. 
 
Reasons for
Decision
This decision will allow continued access to
the pan-London Sexual Health eService (SHL.UK). This will allow the
Council to benefit from the outcome of the procurement
process, led by the City of London Corporation (CoLC), which will secure online sexual health
services for London residents. The service offers residents of
participating London Boroughs accessible online sexual health
assessments, home testing kits for sexually transmitted infections
(STIs), a clinical results service and remote treatment for common,
uncomplicated cases of bacterial infections such as chlamydia and
Trichomonas Vaginalis (TV).

safe, contributing positively to their community and developing

Revenue

proposed General Fund net budget requirement of £282.666m

10)

pressures and investments for 2026/2027 to 2028/29 set out in

11)

costs and liabilities, while maintaining adequate cash balances for

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Communities
content:
Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Communities has
approved the transition of the Community Priorities Programme
(CPP) Round 4 into a three-year delivery programme to support
longer-term community
impact, meaning that three-year grants will
be allocated at the start of the process to
provide stability and enable organisations to plan and
deliver sustained outcomes. The Cabinet Member has also approved
the transition of CPP into a business-as-usual programme, and the
proposal for the programme to transition from 13 delivery wards to
12 delivery wards and recognise the change in the prioritised
wards based on recent IMD 2025 data. Finally, the Cabinet Member
has delegated authority to the Executive Director for Environment
& Communities to approve the issuing of grant funding to
organisations as part of CPP Round 4.
 
Reasons for
Decision
The Community Priorities
Programme consistently delivers strong social value, reaches
vulnerable communities, and strengthens local leadership.
Approval of the changes to the way in which the programme is
delivered will ensure continuity of the
programme and further enable resident-led
decision-making within city-wide systems.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Communities has decided to transition the Community Priorities Programme into a three-year delivery programme to support longer-term community impact.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector
content:
Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social
Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has
approved Westminster City Council entering into
a Section 75 partnership agreement with the North West London Integrated Care Board for the
period from 1 February 2026 to 31 March 2026 and noted
the retrospective service commencement of the section 75
partnership agreement from 1 April 2025 to 31 January
2026. 
 
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social
Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has also
approved a delegation to the Executive Director for Adult
Social Care to negotiate and finalise the terms of the Section 75
Agreement with the North West London Integrated Care
Board, and to agree any variations to the section 75
agreement, and a delegation to the Executive Director for Adult
Social Care and Health to approve the Council entering into
the section 75 agreement, with the North West London
Integrated Care Board (or successor body) for the period
from 1 April 2026 until 31 March 2027. 
 
Reasons for
Decision
One of the most ambitious programmes ever
introduced across the NHS and local government, the Better Care
Fund (BCF), encourages integration by
requiring ICBs and local authorities to enter
into pooled budget arrangements and agree an integrated
spending plan. The BCF national condition for grant funding is
that a signed Section 75 agreement is in place between
the local authority and the Integrated Care Board (ICB).
topline: The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has decided to approve a Section 75 partnership agreement with the North West London Integrated Care Board.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Finance and Council Reform
content:
Decision Taken: The Cabinet Member for
Finance and Council Reform approved the allocation of
£1m from the corporate risk
reserve to establish a dedicated budget to
support the on-going cyber-incident response and future
recovery work. 
 
Reasons for Decision:
To ensure a dedicated and sufficient budget is in
place as soon as possible to support
the on-going cyber security incident response
and future recovery work. Having a centrally controlled
budget will ensure strong financial governance and
oversight of expenditure related to this work.
 
Urgency: This decision has been taken
through special urgency procedure. This falls under provision
2.1.18 of the Policy and Scrutiny Procedure Rules in the
Council’s Constitution where the Council may apply a case of
special urgency and the call-in procedure shall not apply if any
delay likely to be caused by the call-in process would seriously
prejudice the Council’s or the public’s interests.
Councillor Piddock as Chair of the Committee has been briefed and
has agreed to this course of action. 
 
Further, under provision 1.14 of the Access to
Information Rules, where compliance with the requirements of
publicity in connection with executive decisions (set out at 1.12
in the Council’s Constitution) are impracticable a key
decision can progress under special urgency provided that the
requirements set out in 1.14 are met.
 
Adherence to the normal Policy and Scrutiny
Procedure rules is not practical in these circumstances as the
Council must ensure that a dedicated and sufficient budget is
in place as soon as possible to support the on-going cyber security
incident response and future recovery work. The Chief Executive and
Monitoring Officer are satisfied that this is a necessary use of
the special urgency provision and as such the decision is not
subject to call-in.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Finance and Council Reform has decided to allocate £1m for a dedicated budget to support cyber-incident response and recovery work.

of the City of Westminster On-Street ASB PSPO to take
effect from 00:00hr on 25 February 2026 and run for
3-years to 23:59hr on the 24 February 2029.
 
Reasons for Decision: There is evidence

residents, visitors and businesses in the area will stand
to benefit from improved safety through enforcement
of the order.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
Public Health and Voluntary Sector will consider the
recommendations made after consulting on introducing a charge
to cover the administrative cost of arranging care for self-funders
who request assistance and residents for whom the Council acts as
Appointee for State Benefit.  

Summary of Decision: The Cabinet Member
for Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has
approved the introduction of a£35.28 flat weekly fee for
selffunders to cover the Council’s costs associated with
arranging the self-funders nonresidential care and support needs.
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Public Health and
Voluntary Sector has also approved the introduction of an annual
fee for acting as Appointee for State Benefits. If a person has
between £3,000 and £20,500, they will pay 3.5% of the
value of their assets. If they have more than £20,500, they
will pay £824 per year. No charge will be made if someone has
less than £3,000.
 
Reasons for Decision: Councils can
charge for the administrative costs of providing an arrangement
service for self-funders who ask the Council to arrange their care
at home, and the Council can charge for the administrative costs
when acting as an Appointee for State Benefits. Introducing these
charges would represent a fair means of meeting the administrative
costs incurred by the Council for making these are arrangements,
and safeguard investment in wider adult social care services for
the future.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

Approves
the disposal of a portfolio of temporary
accommodation from those listed in Exempt Appendix
A, from the Council to a Council owned Limited
Liability Partnership. 
Approves the creation of a
structure and arrangements satisfying the Funder’s
criteria. 

Approves entering into the arrangements, to be
agreed with the Security Trustee and the Funder, to secure the
funding, including the Council providing an
unlimited guarantee to the Security Trustee and the
LLP granting security to the Security Trustee over
the Portfolio. The Security Trustee will hold all
security on behalf of the Funder and other secured creditors of the
LLP.
Approves the
Council acquiring a lease(s) (which may
be affected by one or more leases) of
the Portfolio granted by the LLP, following
the disposal of the Portfolio by
the Council to the LLP. 
Approves the authorisation of the
Council’s Section 151 Officer and Monitoring Officer to
issue certificates to the Security Trustee and the Funder, in
the form to be agreed with the Security Trustee and the
Funder, to certify compliance with applicable financial
requirements and legal requirements (amongst other things)
respectively and further authorises that both officers be
indemnified (to the fullest extent allowed) in connection with the
giving of such certificates. 
Delegates authority to the Executive
Director of Finance and Resources in consultation
with the Executive Director of Housing and
Commercial Partnerships to: 



approve the entry into all legal
agreements and associated documentation  
undertake all other necessary
actions to secure the sale
and subsequent leaseback of the Portfolio,
including without limitation, the funding arrangements. 
approve Westminster TA 1 Ltd
and Westminster TA 2 Ltd to be members of the LLP or
the incorporation of other limited companies to be
members of the LLP and the subsequent incorporation
of the LLP to acquire the Portfolio and all
associated bank accounts, governance arrangements, insurance and
other administrative, operational, legal aspects as
required. 


Reasons for Decision:
The Council seeks to secure better
value accommodation to meet the needs of homeless residents
and its statutory obligations, and disposal
of this portfolio will raise a capital receipt to
support the investment of additional homes for use as
temporary accommodation (TA), limit the level of
borrowing required and reduce
ongoing costs.

application for Westminster.
content:
Cabinet will consider the A Westminster
Welcome strategy, which will form part of a full City of Sanctuary
application for Westminster.  
 

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 


That Cabinet approves ‘A Westminster Welcome:
The Strategy for People Seeking Sanctuary in Our
Borough’ (Appendix 1).  

 
Reasons for Decision: This
decision will enable the Council to move from strategy
development to delivery of the Sanctuary Strategy and its
accompanying action plan, which will be an integral part
of the Council’s application to become a
Council of Sanctuary.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve 'A Westminster Welcome: The Strategy for People Seeking Sanctuary in Our Borough' as part of a full City of Sanctuary application for Westminster.

decision_maker: Cabinet
content:
Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

Approves the designation
of the North Paddington High Streets
Area (“the HSRA Designated Area”) and
the use of the High Street Rental Auction
powers by the Council in respect of the HSRA Designated
Area. 
Approves the draw down and
administration of New Burdens Funding from Central
Government to cover a proportion of the costs
of using the High Street Rental Auction
(HSRA) powers in the HSRA Designated Area. 
Delegates authority
to the Executive Director for
Regeneration, Economy and
Planning, following consultation with the Cabinet Member
for Planning and Economic Development, to: 

arrange for registration
of the local land charge for the HSRA
Designated Area. 
implement the use of
the High Street Rental Auction powers and
manage individual high street rental auction(s) in
respect of the HSRA Designated Area, including
the issuing of all notices, licences, orders, entry into
legal
documents and taking other related action
as may be necessary.   



·      
Delegates authority to the Executive Director for
Regeneration, Economy and
Planning, following consultation with the Cabinet Member
for Planning and Economic Development, to
approve future consultation exercises (required by
legislation) for areas in Paddington and
Bayswater, Pimlico,
and any other areas considered for use of
high street rental auction powers. 
 
Reasons for Decision: The adoption of
HSRA powers will provide the Council with an effective statutory
tool to address persistent high street vacancies and support local
economic growth. The powers enable the Council to intervene where
engagement with landlords has not secured positive outcomes,
ensuring that long-term vacant commercial properties can be brought
back into productive use for the benefit of communities and
businesses.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the use of High Street Rental Auction powers in the North Paddington High Streets Area to address high street vacancies and support local economic growth.

content:
Cabinet will consider the appointment of a
supplier to deliver leasing and housing supply opportunities
following a competitive procurement process.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

Approves in principle:
i) entering into
a Bulk Leasing Supply Agreement (“the
Agreement”) for the supply of a maximum
of 300 homes within the Council’s TA
allocations policy Band 1and 2 areas;
and ii) entering into subsequent leases of
properties flowing from the Agreement on lease terms of
10 year and 1 day and other high-level heads of
terms as detailed in Confidential Part B of this
report  
Delegates authority to
the Executive Director of Finance and Resources,
following consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance and
Council Reform, subject to all necessary due
diligence, to agree the final commercial terms
of the Agreement including the final form and
terms of lease to be entered into for all properties
supplied under the Agreement and to enter into
all associated legal agreements and documentation to
effect this arrangement.  

 
Reasons for Decision: The Council
has a statutory obligation to house people in need and
this agreement in principle to enter into
a bulk leasing agreement for the supply of properties for use
by the Council as TA will assist the meeting of this
obligation.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a Bulk Leasing Supply Agreement for the supply of 300 homes to meet the Council's statutory obligation to house people in need.

content:
Council approved the following recommendation:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendation of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendation approved.
 
Resolved:
 
That Full Council
approved:
 
Pursuant to Regulation 26 and
35 of the Town and Country Planning (Local Planning)(England)
Regulations 2012, the adoption of the City Plan Partial Review and
supporting Policies Map in line with the recommendations of the
Inspector’s Report and that the new Local Plan for
Westminster is known as the ‘City Plan 2019- 2040
(2026)’ and replaces the ‘City Plan 2019-2040’
(2021). This includes (but not limited to):
 
i)               
Replacing adopted Policy 9 Affordable Housing with
new Policy 13 Affordable Housing;
ii)             
Inserting Policies 8 – 11 (site allocations);
and
iii)             
Inserting Policy 43 Retrofit first.
 
Reasons for Decision:
 
1)
       To
enable the Council to manage the sustainable development of
Westminster by adopting the policies in the City Plan Partial
Review and the Policies Map pursuant to Regulation 26 and 35 of the
Town and Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations
2012.
 
2)
       The City
Plan Partial Review policies will ensure opportunities for
affordable housing delivery are maximised and that most new
affordable homes are for social rent, in line with updated housing
needs evidence. The new Retrofit First policy will ensure
developers consider a retrofit-first approach to development, and
that any demolition works are justified. The new site allocation
policies will help unlock development on four underutilised sites
in the city, therefore promoting sustainable development and the
delivery of new homes, jobs, open and green spaces and the
infrastructure needed to support the city.
topline: The Council has decided to adopt the City Plan Partial Review and supporting Policies Map in Westminster.

content:
Council approved the following recommendations:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendations of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendations approved.
 
Resolved:
 
1) That
Full Council approved the following recommendations for the
financial year 2026/27:
 
(i)             
that the Council does not set a Council Tax discount
for either empty properties or second homes and instead a Long-Term
Empty Property Premium and Second Home Premium continue at the
maximum levels allowed for by the current legislation for the
2026/27 financial year.
 
(ii)
      that the
Director of Revenues & Benefits be given delegated authority to
determine any individual local discount applications received from
Council Taxpayers during the 2026/27 financial year under section
13A(1)(c) of the Local Government Finance Act 1992.
 
2) That
Full Council approved the same Council Tax Reduction Scheme for
2026/27 which had operated successfully since 2013/14. The scheme
was based on the Default Scheme Regulations, updated to reflect
changes made via the Prescribed Requirements Amendment Regulations
and with War Disabled Pensions, War Widow, Pensions and Armed
Forces Compensation scheme payments disregarded in full when
calculating a claimant’s income. The same disregards should
continue to apply to Housing Benefit and claims for Discretionary
Housing Payment (DHP).
 
3)
       That
Full Council resolved that the Council Tax Base for 2026/27 for the
Whole City was 154,862.86 equivalent Band D properties, for
Montpelier Square alone 113.28 equivalent Band D properties and for
Queen’s Park 3,825.88 equivalent Band D
properties.
 
4)
       That
Full Council resolved that the figures set out in paragraph 3 above
for the Council Tax Base for 2026/27 be used by the Council to make
a determination pursuant to the requirements of the Local
Government Finance Act 1992.
 

Reasons for Decision:
 
1)
       The
taxbase decision is sought in order that the Council complies with
the requirements of the Local Government Finance Act
1992.
 
2)
       The
retention of the same levels of Council Tax discount, for empty
properties and second homes will continue to deliver additional
Council Tax income for the Council without disadvantaging any
vulnerable members of the community.
3)
       The
recommendation to allow the Director of Revenues and Benefits to
continue to determine any individual local discount claims will
enable assistance to be given to individual Council Taxpayers. This
will provide the mechanism for granting the local Council Tax
discount for Care Leavers, foster carers, and other vulnerable
Council Taxpayers in line with the Council’s Council Tax
Ethical Recovery procedure.
 
4)
       The
Council’s proposed 100% Council Tax Reduction Scheme will
mean that the level of Council Tax support provided to the
borough’s working age claimants will effectively mirror that
previously provided under the national Council Tax Benefit scheme
and will also mirror the same level of statutory support provided
to the borough’s pensioners.
 
5)
       The
recommendation to continue the Long-Term Empty Property Premium and
Second Home Premium at the maximum levels allowed for within
current legislation aligns with the Council’s aim to bring
properties back in to use for residents, as well as delivering
additional income for the council, without effecting vulnerable
residents.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for Council Tax discounts and reduction schemes for the financial year 2026/27.

content:
Council approved the following recommendation:
 
The Lord Mayor put the
recommendation of the report to the vote and on a show of hands
declared the recommendations approved.
 
Resolved:
 
That Full Council approved the
proportional division of seats on the Standing Committees as set
out in the report.
 
Reason for Decision:
 
The Local Government and
Housing Act 1989 requires local authorities, where Members are
divided into political groups, to review the proportional division
of seats on Standing Committees following changes in political
group membership to ensure political balance.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the proportional division of seats on Standing Committees.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the Council Tax taxbase,
reduction scheme and discounts for the following financial
year.
content:
Cabinet will consider the Council Tax taxbase,
reduction scheme and discounts for the following financial
year.

Cabinet approved the following
recommendations to Full Council for consideration at its
meeting on 4 March 2026:
 

Approve that the Council does not
set a Council Tax discount for either empty properties or second
homes and instead a Long-Term Empty Property Premium and Second
Home Premium continue at the maximum levels allowed for by the
current legislation for the 2026/27 financial year.
Delegate authority to Director of
Revenues & Benefits be given delegated authority to determine
any individual local discount applications received from Council
Taxpayers during the 2026/27 financial year under section 13A(1)(c)
of the Local Government Finance Act 1992.
Approves the same Council Tax
Reduction Scheme for 2026/27 which has operated successfully since
2013/14. The scheme is based on the Default Scheme Regulations,
updated to reflect changes made via the Prescribed Requirements
Amendment Regulations and with War Disabled Pensions, War Widow,
Pensions and Armed Forces Compensation scheme payments disregarded
in full when calculating a claimant’s income. The same
disregards should continue to apply to Housing Benefit and claims
for Discretionary Housing Payment (DHP).
Resolves that the Council Tax Base
for 2026/27 for the Whole City is 154,862.86 equivalent Band D
properties, for Montpelier Square alone 113.28 equivalent Band D
properties and for Queen’s Park 3,825.88 equivalent Band D
properties. 2.5. Resolves that the figures set out in paragraph 2.3
above for the Council Tax Base for 2026/27 be used by the Council
to make a determination pursuant to the
requirements of the Local Government Finance Act 1992. 

 
Reasons for
Decision:

The taxbase decision is sought in
order that the Council complies with the requirements of the Local
Government Finance Act 1992.
The retention of the same levels of
Council Tax discount, for empty properties and second homes will
continue to deliver additional Council Tax income for the Council
without disadvantaging any vulnerable members of the
community.
The recommendation to allow the
Director of Revenues and Benefits to continue to determine any
individual local discount claims will enable 88 assistance to be given to individual Council
Taxpayers. This will provide the mechanism for granting the local
Council Tax discount for Care Leavers, foster carers, and other
vulnerable Council Taxpayers in line with the Council’s
Council Tax Ethical Recovery procedure.
The Council’s proposed 100%
Council Tax Reduction Scheme will mean that the level of Council
Tax support provided to the borough’s working age claimants
will effectively mirror that previously provided under the national
Council Tax Benefit scheme and will also mirror the same level of
statutory support provided to the borough’s pensioners.
The recommendation to continue the
Long-Term Empty Property Premium and Second Home Premium at the
maximum levels allowed for within current legislation aligns with
the Council’s aim to bring properties back in to use for
residents, as well as delivering additional income for the council,
without effecting vulnerable residents.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve Council Tax discounts and schemes for the upcoming financial year, impacting various stakeholders in the community.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the partial freehold
disposal of Cavendish Square Gardens and Cavendish Square Car
Park.
content:
Cabinet will consider the partial freehold
disposal of Cavendish Square Gardens and Cavendish Square Car
Park.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

Approve: 2.1.1. the appropriation of
the Property for planning purposes
Delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Finance and Resources to:

approve the freehold and leasehold
disposals of the land described in the legal and governance section
of this report including:

i) the disposal to the Buyer of part
of the Council’s freehold estate of land which includes the
Car Park in accordance with the Heads of Terms; noting there has
been a change in the Buyer from the previous terms, with the
details provided in confidential Appendix B of this report; 7
ii) the grant to the Buyer of a
short occupational lease of no more than seven years in respect of
the Gardens in accordance with the Heads of Terms.


approve any non-substantial
variations to the commercial terms. The Heads of Terms are provided
in the confidential appendix to the First Report and it is noted in
this report there has been a change in the Buyer from the previous
terms, with the details provided in confidential Appendix C of this
report.
agree the terms and conditions of,
and enter into the conditional option/agreement for lease for the
following provided they are in accordance with the Heads of Terms
including:

(a) approve an early surrender of
the Car Park lease by way of agreement;
(b) the freehold disposal of part of
the Property to the Buyer by way of a transfer deed;
(c) the grant of an occupational
lease to the Buyer for a term not exceeding seven years enabling it
to close, use for construction purposes and undertake works to the
Gardens;
(d) any agreement for the future
management or maintenance of the Gardens;
(e) any further legal documentation
that may be necessary to facilitate the transactions; and
(f) on completion of the proposed
works, in so far as may be deemed necessary, to appropriate the
Gardens for open space purposes.


undertake the necessary accounting
and financial due diligence on the Buyer and transactions as
necessary
Apply on behalf of the Council as
landowner for the required consent under section 3 of the 1931
Act.



 
Reasons for
Decision:
 

This report recommends that the
Property be appropriated for planning purposes and thereafter,
disposed of under planning powers to enable the proposed
development to proceed.
Members are referred to section 5 of
the First Report which describes the factors relevant to a decision
to appropriate land for planning purposes in accordance 8 with
section 122 of the Local Government Act 1972 and to dispose of land
in accordance with section 233 of the Town and Country Planning Act
1990.
In particular, paragraph 5.38 of the
First Report summarises the planning justification for the
proposals, based on a review of the reasons for the grant of
planning permission (reference 19/08460/FULL) for the development.
It concludes that the overall transaction would facilitate the
redevelopment of the Car Park and improvement works to the Gardens,
which would in turn improve the economic, social and environment
wellbeing of the area around the Property and the City of
Westminster and secure the long-term future of the Gardens. Such
public benefits would not arise if the Council retained the
Property in its current form. While the Gardens will be temporarily
closed during the carrying out of the development, in the longer
term the improved Gardens will be held for planning purposes for
use as open space for the public to enjoy.
The statutory protection of the
Gardens as a “protected square” aimed at safeguarding
the open space for enjoyment by the public, and the need for
separate consent to enable works affecting the Gardens to proceed
are noted above and in section 7 of this report.
An equality impact assessment has
been prepared for these proposals and appears at Appendix B2 to the
First Report. It has been reviewed once more but remains
unchanged.
With regard to the proposed land
disposals, the commercial and financial implications of the
proposals are set out in this report. Members are referred to
section 4, the Heads of Terms in Exempt Appendix C and section 6.
If the proposals proceed, the disposal of the Car Park will result
in a healthcare-led development and improvement works to the
Gardens. A General Fund capital receipt of £42m will be
generated and the transactions will ensure a commercially
beneficial outcome for an underperforming asset for the
Council.
The proposed terms of the
transaction include contractual safeguards for the Council in the
event of default or non-performance by the Buyer including as
regards the maintenance of the Gardens, their accesses and support
from the subterranean space. The statutory protection of the
Gardens under the 1931 Act, has been taken into account in devising
the structure of the proposals.
Implications of implementation of
the proposals would also include the following:

i. Closure of the Gardens for a
period of up to seven years to enable construction with a temporary
negative impact on users but with three alternative open spaces
within a 0.4 radius and the benefit of enabling improvements to the
features of the Gardens and public safety in the longer term;
ii. Positive impact on the local and
wider London economy, support for environmental aspirations
including the reduction in vehicle movements and significant
employment opportunities in the construction phase;
iii. Certainty for the Council in
respect of the car park, about which there are concerns regarding
its financial and operational performance, and its replacement with
a healthcare-led development providing access to further medical
facilities; iv. Benefit to the Council’s capital financing
position, best consideration for the disposal of Council land
realisation of planning obligations and CIL contributions to be
reinvested in the local infrastructure.



In the event that the Council decides, having
considered this report, not to appropriate the Property or dispose
of parts of the land, the conditional contract/agreement for lease
will not proceed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the partial freehold disposal of Cavendish Square Gardens and Cavendish Square Car Park for a proposed development, despite potential contentious issues surrounding the temporary closure of the Gardens and commercial implications.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
Public Health and Voluntary Sector will consider the implementation
of the Anti-Poverty Action Plan (2025–2028) and Food Plan
(2025–2028) — two complementary plans designed to
address poverty, tackle inequality, and improve social,
environmental and economic wellbeing for residents.
content:
The Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
Public Health and Voluntary Sector will consider the implementation
of the Anti-Poverty Action Plan (2025–2028) and Food Plan
(2025–2028) — two complementary plans designed to
address poverty, tackle inequality, and improve social,
environmental and economic wellbeing for residents. 

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
 

Approve the Westminster Anti-Poverty
Action Plan (2026–2030) and Food Plan as set out in
Appendices A and B.
Delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Finance and Resources & the Executive Director of
Environment & Communities in consultation with the Cabinet
Member to make minor amendments to respective plans as
required

 
Reasons for
Decision:
 

Addressing inequality is a key
priority for the Council. The Poverty in Westminster analysis
highlights significant disparities in income, employment, housing,
and health across the city.
Tackling poverty is not only a
matter of social equity but a preventative investment, reducing
long-term demand and costs across housing, children’s
services, and community safety.
The ongoing Fair Funding Review may
affect local government allocations, potentially reducing
Westminster’s financial flexibility. A coordinated
Anti-Poverty and Food Plan is therefore essential to ensure that
resources are targeted effectively and deliver the greatest
possible impact for residents most in need.

 
Both plans create a clear framework for
addressing inequality and together support a coordinated approach
across departments for tackling poverty and food-related issues.
Their implementation will align resources with council priorities,
ensure effective resource allocation and enable transparent
monitoring and reporting of measurable results.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Anti-Poverty Action Plan and Food Plan to address inequality and poverty in Westminster.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector
content:
Decision Taken: The Cabinet Member for
Adult Social Care, Public Health and Voluntary Sector has approved
the procurement strategy for a new contract delivering the Carers
Hub service, commencing on 1st April 2026 for an initial period of
five (5) years until 31st March 2031, with two proposed extension
periods of an additional two (2) years (up to 31st March 2033) and
a further two (2) years (up to 31st March 2035), for a total value
of £3,834,000 (including both extension periods).
 
Reasons for Decision: The Carers Hub
Service is currently in operation and continues to deliver the
services as described in 1.2; the current contract is now due to
expire on 31st March 2026. There are no permitted options to extend
this contract arrangement. A review of the existing service has
taken place, and a revised specification produced, with the aim to
carry out a procurement of new bi-borough services in Autumn 2025,
with new contracts awarded in February 2026. A competitive tender
process to test the market is recommended and the procurement
strategy proposes an Open tender, via the Procurement Act 2023.

Cabinet will consider the approval of a
strategy to improve night-time life, aiming for a safe, vibrant,
inclusive, and sustainable experience for various users. 

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Approves the Westminster After Dark Strategy 2025-2040
(Appendix 1).

·      
Approves the accompanying Implementation Plan (Appendix 2).
 
Reasons for Decision
The WAD
Strategy and Implementation Plan is presented for approval
following extensive engagement and consultation with residents,
businesses, and key stakeholders across Westminster. The strategy
reflects the outcomes of this consultation and engagement activity
over a number of years, ensuring that it
is evidence-based, balanced and responds to community
priorities.

Council to move from strategy development to delivery.

Cabinet will consider a procurement strategy
for the award of a new contract for Waste and Recycling
Collections, Street Cleansing and Winter Maintenance.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
Approves the procurement strategy outlined in
this report.
 
Reasons for
Decision
The
current contract delivered by Veolia ends on 15 September 2027. To
enable a procurement of the new contract, agreement for the
procurement strategy is needed.

 

Agreement will facilitate the procurement process to enable
Westminster City Council (WCC) to continue to deliver its statutory
obligations under the Environmental Protection Act 1990. It will
also enable WCC to deliver its own priorities under the Fairer
Westminster Strategy.
 
A new
contract will provide an opportunity to update the requirements,
processes, and procedures to deliver current and future
services.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the recommendations made
by the North Paddington Serious Violence Taskforce, and detail how
the Council plans to respond to the recommendations.
content:
Cabinet will consider the recommendations made
by the North Paddington Serious Violence Taskforce, and detail how
the Council plans to respond to the recommendations.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Approves the Council's response to the recommendations of the North
Paddington Serious Violence Taskforce as set out in Appendix 2.

·      
Approves the initial spend of £150,000 to implement the
Council's response to the recommendations of the North Paddington
Serious Violence Taskforce, as specified in paragraph 4.9.

·      
Delegates authority to the Cabinet Member for Communities to
approve the further spend of up to £100,000 to implement the
Council's response to the recommendations of the North Paddington
Serious Violence Taskforce.
 
Reasons for Decision
The North
Paddington Serious Violence Taskforce has identified key areas for
the Council, other public agencies, the voluntary and community
sectors, and communities themselves to work together on. The
Council's response to the recommendations suggests piloting new,
place-based approaches to respond to the issue of serious
violence.
 
By approving
the spend allocated to implementing the Council's response to the
Taskforce's recommendations, the Council will drive forward both,
its response to serious violence in North Paddington and its
contribution towards the systems change that the communities in the
area have asked the Council for.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations from the North Paddington Serious Violence Taskforce and allocate funds to implement the Council's response to address serious violence in the community.

content:
Cabinet will consider a recommended service
delivery model for the delivery of repairs and maintenance services
to Council homes, following the expiry of the current term
partnership arrangements in 2027-28. 
 

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:
Approves the
establishment of a Strategic Alliance underpinned by the Framework
Alliance Contract
(FAC-1) as a
strategic framework for the contracts set out in this report.
 
Delegates authority
to the Executive Director of Housing & Commercial Partnerships,
in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Housing Services,
to:

(i)             
Approve the procurement strategies for each contract as set out in
Table 2 and Section 11 of this report; and

(ii)            
Take any necessary steps to implement the Strategic Alliance
including implementing the individual procurement strategies,
subsequently procuring any consultants, contractors or providers to
support the delivery and operation of the Strategic Alliance, and
entering into any legal or other agreements to give effect to these
recommendations.
 
Reasons for Decision
The current
Term Partnering Contracts (TPC) expire in 2027.

 
The proposed
Strategic Alliance Framework and contract delivery model represents
a transformative approach to service delivery, placing resident
experience, sustainability, and collaboration at its core. It
aligns with the Council’s long-term strategic goals and
equips the Housing Service to address current and future challenges
effectively.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to establish a Strategic Alliance for repairs and maintenance services to Council homes post-2027, aiming to transform service delivery and align with long-term strategic goals.

decision_maker: Leader of the Council
content:
Summary of Decision 
 
The Leader of the Council approves the
nomination for a Westminster Commemorative Green Plaque to mark the
former headquarters of the Football Association at 22 Lancaster
Gate 
 
Reasons for Decision 
 
The nomination is supported by the independent
Green Plaque panel in recognition of the cultural and historical
significance of the Football Association, the amount of time
located at Lancaster Gate and the significant events in the history
of English football which took place in the building. Lancaster
Gate became synonymous with the Football Association and the
tradition and authority of English football.  
The Green Plaque panel is an independent
advisory panel who review all submissions to provide informal
approval ahead of the Cabinet Member Report. Panel members are
Rachel Anthony, The City of Westminster Guide Lecturers
Association; Helen Glew, Senior Lecturer in History, University of
Westminster; Gillian Staples, Archives, Collections & Resources
Lead, Westminster City Council and Colin Thom, Senior Research
Associate, Survey of London, UCL Faculty of the Built
Environment.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve the nomination for a Westminster Commemorative Green Plaque at 22 Lancaster Gate.

Cabinet will consider the freehold
sale of Cavendish Square Carpark and Gardens.
content:
Cabinet will consider the freehold
sale of Cavendish Square Carpark and Gardens.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Noted the draft commercial terms as set out in this report and the
Heads of Terms at Appendix C.

·      
Approved proceeding with the advertising requirements of Section
122(2A) of the 1972 Act and Section 233(4) of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 giving notice of the intended appropriation of
the Property and disposals of parts of the Property.
 
Reasons for Decision: The Council is
proposing to dispose to Reef part of the Council’s freehold
estate of land which includes the Car Park; and grant to Reef of a
short occupational lease (no more than 7 years) of Cavendish Square
Gardens to enable the redevelopment and improvement works to be
carried out. A decision on the proposed appropriation and disposals
of parts of the Property cannot be taken until any objections to
the proposals, in so far as they affect open space land, have been
considered. To meet the requirements of Section 122 of the Local
Government Act 1972, which enables the Council to appropriate land
held for one purpose for another, Cabinet is being asked to approve
proceeding with advertising of the Property.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to proceed with the sale of Cavendish Square Carpark and Gardens, sparking potential controversy over the future use of the public land.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the full business case
for Church Street Site A.
content:
Cabinet will consider the full business case
for Church Street Site A.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Approved and endorsed the Church Street Site A Full Business Case annexed at exempt Appendix A
and the delivery of Church Street Site A by the JV LLP.

·      
Approved expenditure to the JV LLP from the Council’s Housing
Revenue Account of: i. A maximum of £84.100m in Residual Land
Value payment (as detailed in exempt Part B of this Report). ii. A
maximum of £17.844m Social Rent Home Package Price payments
(as detailed in exempt Part B of this Report).

·      
Approved expenditure to the JV LLP from the Council’s General
Fund of: i.
A maximum of £20.000m equity (as detailed in exempt Part B of
this Report). ii. A maximum of £6.208m for the Intermediate
Rent Homes Package Price payments, which will be transferred to
Westminster Builds when complete (as detailed in exempt Part B of
this Report).
 
Reasons for Decision: The development
of Church Street Site A is set to deliver new homes including an
increase of new affordable homes (over 50% increase on the previous
estate), which will include new family sized homes and an increase
of public realm and play space. The FBC represents the final
business case stage for Church Street Site A and reconfirms that a
joint venture partnership delivery route as structured, remains the
most suitable option for delivery. Once the Development Agreement
becomes unconditional, Church Street Site A will be let to the JV
LLP and the JV LLP will commence
delivery of its business plan and the development of Church Street
Site A.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the full business case for Church Street Site A and allocate expenditure for its development.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Cabinet will consider the Outline Business
Case for the Pimlico District Heat Undertaking.
content:
Cabinet will consider the Outline Business
Case for the Pimlico District Heat Undertaking.

Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Approved the proposed shortlist, comprising the four best-scoring
options and the best performing Direct Electric option, for
progression to Full OBC. The recommended shortlist consists of:
o  
Do minimum - pipework replacement
o  
Centralised River Source Heat Pump (RSHP) and Gas Boiler (GB), as
top up and back up, in Churchill Gardens (CG)
o  
Centralised River Source Heat Pump (RSHP) and Electric Boiler (EB),
as top up and back up, in Churchill Gardens (CG)
o  
Cory Mobile Heat Batteries (MHB)
o  
Direct Electric (DE) Variation 3: Storage Heaters and Direct
Cylinders1

·      
Noted that a further report will be brought back to Cabinet seeking
approval of the OBC, the recommended single preferred option, and
any additional funding which may be needed to progress to Full
Business Case.
 
 
Reasons for Decision: There is a strong
strategic case for renewal or replacement of PDHU. The recommended
options are the four highest scoring across a range of Critical
Success Factors, balancing affordability, disruption,
deliverability and wider strategic objectives. Cabinet Members have
also requested to advance the best performing Direct Electric
option to ensure a non-network option is explored further. Approval
of the shortlist of options will allow the programme team to focus
resources on the most viable solutions, progress technical,
commercial and financial analysis, and prepare the Outline Business
Case for Cabinet consideration.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a shortlist of options for the Pimlico District Heat Undertaking, including heat pump and boiler options, mobile heat batteries, and direct electric variations.

decision_maker: Cabinet
content:
Cabinet approved the
following recommendations:

·      
Noted the current position regarding Oxford Street proposals and
recent developments

·      
Confirmed what further action, if any, is to be taken in response
to the petition.
 
Reasons for Decision: A number of
commitments from the Greater London Authority (GLA) have already
been achieved by the Council as part of the transformation of
Oxford Street that will address concerns of residents. The Council
is not aware of any current basis to enable a judicial review
challenge to be made which would have any chance of success. The
proposals will continue to be monitored to ensure that due regard
is paid by the Mayor and the GLA to the issues which the Council
has raised in its consultation response
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations regarding Oxford Street proposals and recent developments.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Communities
content:
Summary of
Decision
The Cabinet Member for Communities has
approved the variation to the Leisure Management Contract with
Sports and Leisure Management Limited, trading as Everyone Active
(SLM) This variation will allow SLM to operate the leisure centres
as an agent rather than as a principal for the purpose of
collecting income from public services. 
 
Reason for
Decision
This will enable Westminster City Council to
benefit from an improved VAT position by moving to an Agency
operating model, under which the Council provides leisure services
through its agent SLM.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Communities has decided to approve the variation to the Leisure Management Contract with Everyone Active, allowing them to operate leisure centres as an agent for collecting income from public services.
